item.description: The Pasadena Design Commission is scheduled Tuesday to review a proposed five-story residential care facility that would bring 145 senior living units to the edge of the Pasadena Playhouse District, adjacent to the historic First Church of Christ, Scientist. item.title: Bay Area Firm Acquires Pasadena’s Vantage Wealth, a $721 Million Advisory
item.description: Vantage Wealth, a Pasadena investment firm that has managed money for local families since 1993, has been acquired by Bay Area-based Summitry, the companies announced earlier this month. Financial terms were not disclosed. The deal brings Vantage Wealth’s $721 million in client assets under the umbrella of Summitry, a Foster City firm managing $3.36 billion, according to a joint press release. item.title: Pasadena Heat Peaks Friday Before Weekend Cooldown
item.description: Warm, sunny conditions will continue in Pasadena through midweek before a cooling trend arrives Sunday, according to the National Weather Service. Highs are expected to reach near 90 degrees Friday and Saturday before dropping into the low 80s early next week. Forecasters said Tuesday’s high will reach 82 degrees under clear skies, with calm winds shifting to light south-southwest breezes in the afternoon. Overnight lows will fall to 55 degrees. item.title: Oak Knoll Project Draws Resident Backlash
item.description: A proposed development at 511 S. Oak Knoll Ave. drew opposition ahead of Monday’s City Council hearing. Residents submitted extensive correspondence raising concerns about design, environmental impacts and neighborhood safety. The project calls for a four-story, 46-unit multifamily building totaling more than 56,000 square feet, with one level of subterranean parking on a roughly 38,000-square-foot site. item.title: ArtCenter’s Iconic Pasadena Bridge Building Turns 50, Prompting College’s First Gala in a Decade
item.description: The modernist steel-and-glass building that spans an arroyo in Pasadena’s San Rafael Hills — and has served as ArtCenter College of Design’s Hillside Campus for half a century — will be the backdrop for the college’s first gala in more than a decade on Saturday, April 18. item.title: Pasadena Wins $500,000 County Grant to Study Lower Arroyo Seco Improvements
item.description: The city has secured a $500,000 grant from Los Angeles County to fund a planning and feasibility study for the Lower Arroyo Seco, a 37-acre natural corridor that stretches from the Colorado Street Bridge to the La Loma Bridge. item.title: Two Tenant Seats on Pasadena’s Rent Board Remain Open After Resignations
item.description: The board that controls how much landlords can raise rents in Pasadena is short two members, and the city is looking for tenants to fill the seats.
